```text
(Produced from a Google Doc export; lines exceed 45 characters)
```
The editor wants a fix that also works when burning captions into a 1:1 Instagram export.
scenario_questions.task: Identify all issues in the SRT and provide a corrected 2-cue excerpt. Then specify export settings for (a) YouTube with sidecar and (b) Instagram with burn-in, including any text layout adjustments for readability/safe area.
scenario_questions.expected_answer:
Issues: (1) SRT uses dot decimals; SRT requires commas. (2) Overlapping timings (cue 2 starts before cue 1 ends). (3) Potentially excessive line length for small square frames. Correction example:

scenario_questions.scenario: A stakeholder asks for a quick swap of a product shot across all three deliverables (YouTube 16:9 + SRT, IG 1:1 burn-in, TikTok 9:16 burn-in). Your current project has one master sequence and two auto-reframed duplicates. The deadline is 2 hours, and prior v03 files have already been shared with partners.
scenario_questions.task: Outline a controlled revision plan that ensures the swap is consistent in all aspect ratios, guarantees filenames don’t collide with v03, and reduces the risk of missing the caption update. Include how you’ll validate the change and what you’ll submit.
scenario_questions.expected_answer: Plan: Replace the product shot in the 16:9 master, ripple as needed, then open the 1:1 and 9:16 reframed sequences to update Auto Reframe segments and add manual position keyframes if required. Update the caption segment timing if the swap changed durations. Batch export using platform-specific presets with incremented versions (v04) and platform/AR in names. Validate by (1) scrubbing through the changed region in all three AR timelines, (2) checking burned-in caption alignment for IG/TikTok and the sidecar timing for YouTube, (3) confirming MediaInfo duration matches within 1–2 frames across variants, and (4) visually confirming the new product shot appears in all three files. Deliverables: three v04 files plus the updated YouTube .srt, leaving prior v03 files intact for partners.

rubric.criterion: Describes consistent update across master and reframed sequences, including manual reframe checks
Versioning and naming plan that prevents overwriting prior deliveries (e.g., v04)
Caption update procedure (sidecar timing and burn-in alignment)
Validation steps that are concrete and time-feasible within 2 hours

practical_tasks.title: Multi-platform export set
practical_tasks.brief: From your capstone edit (or a 30–60 second sequence you created in this course), produce three deliverables for different platforms: YouTube 16:9 with a sidecar SRT, Instagram 1:1 with burned-in captions, and TikTok 9:16 with burned-in captions. Reframe intelligently so subjects remain centered and no unintended pillar/letterboxing appears in the square/vertical cuts.
practical_tasks.deliverable: Multi-platform exports: three video files (MP4/H.264) named with platform and aspect ratio, plus one .srt file for the YouTube deliverable.
acceptance_criteria: Each file’s resolution and aspect ratio are correct: 1920x1080 (16:9), 1080x1080 (1:1), 1080x1920 (9:16).
YouTube file has no burned-in captions and is accompanied by a valid .srt with comma decimals and non-overlapping cues.
Instagram and TikTok files have captions burned in and visibly clear above typical UI (not within the bottom 15% of the frame).
No unintended letterbox/pillarbox in the 1:1 and 9:16 exports; framing keeps key subjects in view.
MediaInfo (or properties) shows Rec.709 tagging on all files.
Filenames include project, platform, aspect ratio, and version (e.g., project_YouTube_16x9_vXX.mp4).

rubric.criterion: Correct technical specs for all three files (resolutions, Rec.709 tagging, codecs)
Captions compliance (YouTube sidecar validity; Instagram/TikTok clean burn-in and placement)
Reframing quality (subjects kept in frame; no unintended letterbox/pillarbox)
File naming/versioning clarity and presence of the required .srt for YouTube
Basic QC evidence in the files (no obvious export glitches, durations consistent across variants)

practical_tasks.title: Finished portfolio video
practical_tasks.brief: Using the provided brief below, finalize a 45–60 second portfolio piece that demonstrates your editing and delivery skills. Integrate on-screen captions and design the cut so a call-to-action appears by 5 seconds. Deliver one master in 16:9 (1080p). The brief: Audience = prospective clients on YouTube/LinkedIn; Tone = confident, concise; Must-have shots = product hero, 2 customer reactions, logo outro; CTA by 00:05.000; Music bed allowed, no profanity.
practical_tasks.deliverable: Finished portfolio video: one mastered MP4 (1920x1080, 45–60s) containing the final cut. Any case-study context and revision summary must be visible inside the video (e.g., brief title card and a 2–3 slide outro) so the assessor can verify by watching the file.
acceptance_criteria: Single MP4 file, 1920x1080, 45–60s total duration.
CTA appears on-screen no later than 00:05.000.
Legible captions are present throughout and do not collide with safe areas; they can be stylistic but must be readable.
Contains the must-have shots: product hero, 2 distinct customer reactions, logo outro.
Includes a short, readable overlay sequence that states the brief in 1–2 lines at the start and a 1–2 slide outro that lists at least one revision you made and why.
Audio and picture are in sync; no unintended black frames or flash frames at in/out; export tagged Rec.709.
Filename includes project name and version (e.g., portfolioMaster_v02.mp4).

Caption presence and legibility across the piece (placement, readability)
Overall edit quality and coherence appropriate for portfolio (pacing, shot choice)

Technical delivery quality (1080p, Rec.709, clean in/out, sync)
